cases.title: Piano Key Click Audio and Active State Highlight
cases.description: Verify that clicking a visible piano key plays the corresponding audio file from the tunes directory, applies the 'active' class immediately, and removes the 'active' class after 150ms.

cases.title: Volume Slider Adjustment
cases.description: Verify that adjusting the volume slider updates the audio output instantly across its range from 0 (mute) to 1 (maximum volume).

cases.title: Show Keys Checkbox Toggle Visibility
cases.description: Verify that interacting with the 'Show Keys' checkbox toggles the visibility of key labels by adding or removing the 'hide' class across all piano keys, and handles rapid toggling consistently.

cases.title: Piano Key Elements and Default Layout Rendering
cases.description: Verify that all required white and black piano keys are correctly rendered inside a <ul> with class 'piano-keys' with proper attributes, nested span labels, and default visibility along with the checkbox input.

cases.title: Keyboard Press and Mouse Click Parity
cases.description: Verify that physical keyboard presses corresponding to the key labels trigger the same audio playback, active class highlighting, and behavior as mouse clicks.

opinions.feedback: The proposed high-level test cases are well-structured, distinct, cover all requirements accurately, and are fully testable without any blockers.
All requirements and test cases are well-defined, clear, and fully testable. No blockers identified.

analysis.analysis: e2edev_bench_06-R-1: Testable behaviors include clicking visible piano keys identified by data-testid (e.g., 'piano-key-a', 'piano-key-w'), playing the correct audio file from 'tunes/' directory, applying the 'active' class immediately on click, and removing the 'active' class after exactly 150ms. Boundaries involve rapid successive clicks on the same or different keys. Normal path is clicking a key, hearing the audio, and seeing the temporary highlight. Abnormal paths include missing audio files or concurrent overlapping plays. Ambiguities: handling of rapid re-clicks on an active key before 150ms elapses. e2edev_bench_06-R-3: Testable behaviors include adjusting the volume slider (data-testid='volume-slider') within a range of 0 to 1, updating the audio output instantly, muting at 0, and maxing volume at 1. Boundaries: slider values exactly at 0 and 1, values outside range if manually set. Normal path: dragging or changing slider value updates volume instantly. Abnormal paths: invalid or non-numeric slider values. Ambiguities: none. e2edev_bench_06-R-4: Testable behaviors include toggling the 'Show Keys' checkbox (data-testid='show-keys-checkbox'), adding/removing the 'hide' class on all piano keys (data-testid starting with 'piano-key'). Boundaries: rapid toggling back and forth. Normal path: default state is visible (labels shown), checking hides labels ('hide' class added), unchecking restores labels ('hide' class removed). Abnormal paths: rapid concurrent toggle events. Ambiguities: initial state synchronization if checkbox state differs from default DOM state. e2edev_bench_06-R-5: Testable behaviors include rendering all required white and black piano keys with labels ('a', 'w', 's', 'e', 'd', 'f', 't', 'g', 'y', 'h', 'u', 'j', 'k', 'o', 'l', 'p', ';') inside a <ul> with class 'piano-keys'. Each key must be an <li> element with classes 'key' and 'white' or 'black', containing a 'data-key' attribute, a 'data-testid' format 'piano-key-{label}', and a nested <span> for the label. The 'show-keys-checkbox' must be an <input type='checkbox'> with data-testid 'show-keys-checkbox'. Boundaries: presence of all 17 specified keys. Normal path: correct DOM hierarchy loaded by default. Abnormal paths: missing attributes or malformed tags. Ambiguities: none. e2edev_bench_06-R-6: Testable behaviors include triggering the exact same audio playback, active class highlighting, and timing behavior via physical keyboard presses corresponding to data-key values as well as mouse clicks. Boundaries: matching keyboard events (keydown) to their corresponding piano keys. Normal path: pressing key 'a' on the keyboard behaves identically to clicking 'piano-key-a'. Abnormal paths: pressing unmapped keys, holding down keys causing key-repeat events. Ambiguities: whether key-repeat (holding key down) should trigger continuous sounds or single hits.
